entities.summary:
Cathair Mór was a prominent economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in Ireland from approximately 300 BCE to 200 BCE. He was part of a circle of intellectuals who contributed to the development of Irish monastic schools and the preservation of classical knowledge during the Roman Empire's occupation of Ireland.



Cathair Mór's work focused on the intersection of economics, philosophy, and politics, with a particular emphasis on the impact of Roman trade policies on Irish society. His theories on the effects of mercantilism on economic growth and the role of the state in regulating trade have been cited by scholars as influential in the development of Irish economic thought.



Despite his significance in Irish intellectual history, Cathair Mór's life and work remain relatively unknown outside of academic circles. His legacy, however, continues to be felt in the preservation of classical texts and the development of Irish economic thought.



Cathair Mór's contribution to Irish monastic schools can be seen in the numerous inscriptions and manuscripts attributed to him, which have been preserved in libraries and archives throughout Ireland.
